attributes.board_name: New Jersey State Board of Medical Examiners

rules.accepted_credit_types: Category I (min. 40) and Category II (max. 60) recognized by the AMA, AOA, APMA, ACCME or comparable organizations recognized by the board; optional menopause CE counts (P.L. 2025, c. 175)
rules.new_licensee_rule: Initial licensees who completed accredited graduate medical education within 12 months before licensure are exempt for the initial biennial period only.
rules.alternatives: Hardship waiver or extension (illness, disability, military service, etc.) for the current cycle, requested in writing by certified mail at least 60 days before the biennial period ends. Retired (no-fee) and inactive licenses are exempt.
rules.audit_note: Keep CME certificates at least 6 years (and course outlines for cultural competency topics).

topics.who: 2 of the 40 Category I credits in end-of-life care (C.45:9-7.7); waiver possible if not applicable to practice
One-time 6 hours of accredited CME covering 6 board-specified topics; physicians licensed after June 30, 2007 by the end of the next full renewal cycle (N.J.A.C. 13:35-6.25)

All MDs/DOs: 2 credits in sexual misconduct prevention (incl. informed consent for sensitive exams, duty to report, human trafficking identification), due before the close of the 2027 renewal (N.J.A.C. 13:35-6.15(e))

rules.notes: One board licenses MDs and DOs. Biennial renewal; board page cites a biennial period starting July 1, 2013. Sexual misconduct CME (2025 rule): first due by the 2027 renewal, repeat frequency not stated on the board page. Official N.J.A.C. text is only on LexisNexis (not read).
rules.legal_basis: N.J.A.C. 13:35-6.15; N.J.A.C. 13:35-6.25 and N.J.S.A. 45:9-7.2, 7.3 (cultural competency); C.45:9-7.7 (end-of-life)
